title: Root Chakra
name: Muladhar
subtitle: A place to begin.
description: A crimson lotus and an earth square: a visual language of foundation, steadiness, and being here.
reflection: What feels steady in this moment?
steps: Notice the four petals and the square at the centre.
Let the word “earth” suggest something ordinary and dependable.
Name one source of support you can appreciate today.

title: Sacral Chakra
name: Swadhisthana
subtitle: Make room for movement.
description: An orange lotus holds a silver crescent. Water becomes a metaphor for change, receptivity, and creative flow.
reflection: Where could I allow a little more flexibility?
steps: Follow the curved outline of the crescent.
Notice how the six petals repeat around an open centre.
Reflect on one situation that might benefit from a gentler response.

title: Solar Plexus
name: Manipura
subtitle: Give intention a clear shape.
description: Yellow petals gather around a fire triangle: an invitation to contemplate warmth, direction, and purposeful action.
steps: Notice the triangle’s three edges and its downward point.
Choose one modest intention you can describe clearly.
Think of a practical next step that expresses that intention.

title: Heart Chakra
name: Anahata
subtitle: Let the opposites meet.
description: A green lotus surrounds two interlocking triangles. Their balance offers a visual starting point for kindness and connection.
reflection: What would a kind response look like?
steps: Trace one triangle, then the other.
Notice their different directions and the space they share.
Bring to mind a simple act of kindness you could offer.

title: Throat Chakra
name: Bishuddhi
symbol: Sixteen-petalled lotus · circle within a triangle
subtitle: Space for a considered word.
description: Blue petals and a spacious inner circle invite contemplation of listening, expression, and the pause between words.
reflection: What is worth saying—and what is worth hearing?
steps: Rest your gaze on the circle inside the triangle.
Recall a conversation in which listening mattered.
Choose a short, thoughtful sentence you would like to carry forward.

title: Third Eye
name: Agna
subtitle: Notice the lens you bring.
description: Two indigo petals open around a still centre. Agna offers an artistic focus for attention, discernment, and perspective.
reflection: What have I observed, and what have I assumed?
steps: Notice the two petals and their shared centre.
Recall an ordinary moment from your day.
Separate one detail you observed from one meaning you added.

title: Sahasrara
name: Crown Chakra
subtitle: An opening into stillness.
description: Violet gives way to pearl-white in a many-petalled lotus: a closing image for spaciousness, contemplation, and connection.
reflection: What remains when I leave a little space?
steps: Let the many petals form one whole image.
Pause with the image without needing to interpret every detail.
Close by noticing the room around you and one thought to carry with you.
